<reflection>
The first experiment provided kinetic data that many candidate mechanisms fit with very similar negative log-likelihood (NLL) values, indicating poor discrimination. The top mechanisms (M7, M1, M2, etc.) have NLL differences less than 0.05, making them virtually indistinguishable with a single dataset. The aim of the first turn was to establish a baseline, which was achieved, but further experiments are needed to reduce uncertainty across the entire set.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Increasing the catalyst concentration from 0.01 M to 0.05 M while keeping substrate at 1.0 M and no initial product will stress processes that depend on catalyst concentration, such as dimerization (M2, M3, M13, M18, M19) and deactivation pathways involving catalyst (M9, M13, etc.). Mechanisms without catalyst-catalyst interactions (e.g., M1, M7) are expected to show approximately linear scaling with catalyst at low conversion, while those with dimerization or catalyst-dependent deactivation will exhibit nonlinear behavior. This condition avoids saturation or depletion extremes and probes a new regime that should spread out the NLL values across many mechanisms simultaneously, enhancing discrimination across the entire set rather than just the top pair.
</hypothesis>
